description: The figure is a single-panel data table (rendered as an image, black text on white, no plots, micrographs or schematics) titled implicitly by its caption as "The mechanical properties of the investigated samples at different hot-rolling reductions". The table has seven columns with the exact headers: "Rolling states", "Ultimate tensile strength, MPa", "Yield strength, MPa", "Uniform elongation, %", "Total elongation, %", "Reduction of area, %" and "CVN impact energy, J/m2" (printed as J/m²). Three rows correspond to three hot-rolling reductions: HR45, HR68 and HR82. Every cell reports a mean plus a plus-minus uncertainty. Ultimate tensile strength rises monotonically from 861.0 ± 11.0 MPa (HR45) through 922.0 ± 2.0 MPa (HR68) to 976.0 ± 11.0 MPa (HR82), and yield strength rises in parallel from 480.0 ± 0.0 to 577.0 ± 0.0 to 648.0 ± 13.0 MPa. Ductility falls slightly: uniform elongation 52.0 ± 1.0 → 47.0 ± 0.5 → 39.0 ± 0.8 %, total elongation 60.0 ± 1.0 → 57.0 ± 0.0 → 50.0 ± 1.0 %, with reduction of area almost unchanged at 63.0 ± 1.0, 63.0 ± 0.0 and 61.5 ± 0.3 %. CVN impact energy decreases from 133 ± 2.5 to 116 ± 2.8 to 105 ± 1.2 J/m². The table is the quantitative basis for the paper's claim of a strength–ductility–toughness trade-off with increasing hot-rolling reduction.

subfigures.description: Single image of a seven-column, three-row data table of mechanical properties for rolling states HR45, HR68 and HR82; columns are Rolling states, Ultimate tensile strength (MPa), Yield strength (MPa), Uniform elongation (%), Total elongation (%), Reduction of area (%), and CVN impact energy (J/m2). All entries are mean ± uncertainty.

observations.observation: The figure is a table with three data rows labelled HR45, HR68 and HR82 under a 'Rolling states' column.
Column headers as printed are: 'Ultimate tensile strength, MPa', 'Yield strength, MPa', 'Uniform elongation, %', 'Total elongation, %', 'Reduction of area, %', 'CVN impact energy, J/m2'.
Ultimate tensile strength increases with rolling reduction: 861.0 ± 11.0 MPa (HR45), 922.0 ± 2.0 MPa (HR68), 976.0 ± 11.0 MPa (HR82).
Yield strength increases with rolling reduction: 480.0 ± 0.0 MPa (HR45), 577.0 ± 0.0 MPa (HR68), 648.0 ± 13.0 MPa (HR82).
Uniform elongation decreases with rolling reduction: 52.0 ± 1.0 %, 47.0 ± 0.5 %, 39.0 ± 0.8 % for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
Total elongation decreases with rolling reduction: 60.0 ± 1.0 %, 57.0 ± 0.0 %, 50.0 ± 1.0 % for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively.
Reduction of area stays nearly constant across the three rolling states: 63.0 ± 1.0 %, 63.0 ± 0.0 %, 61.5 ± 0.3 %.
CVN impact energy decreases monotonically with rolling reduction: 133 ± 2.5, 116 ± 2.8 and 105 ± 1.2 J/m² for HR45, HR68 and HR82.
Every tabulated value is reported as a mean with a ± uncertainty; the HR45 yield strength and HR68/HR45 total elongation uncertainties are printed as ± 0.0.
The caption states that the table reports the mechanical properties of the investigated samples at different hot-rolling reductions.

The paper abstract states that with hot-rolling reduction increasing from 45% to 82% both yield strength and ultimate tensile strength were effectively enhanced while ductility and toughness only slightly decreased.
